subject: Civil Engineering
title: Dam Monitoring and Instrumentation
description: A micro-lesson that makes Dam Monitoring and Instrumentation usable.

hook.text: A dam looks solid — but invisible changes inside signal trouble long before failure.

buildup.text: Piezometers measure water pressure inside and under the dam — rising pressure means more seepage.

discovery.text: Pendulums measure dam crest deflection — seasonal temperature changes cause predictable sway.

twist.text: Seepage flow is measured continuously — if it increases or becomes turbid, erosion may be active.

climax.text: Modern dams use fiber optic sensors — detecting strain, temperature, and movement in real time.

punchline.text: A dam tells you it's in trouble — if you listen with the right instruments.

quiz.question: What does increasing turbidity in dam seepage indicate?
options: The reservoir water quality is improving
Internal erosion may be carrying soil particles out of the dam — a sign of piping
The dam's drainage system is working more efficiently
